reasoning_traces.think:
AdaER introduces two key mechanisms: C-CMR and E-BRS. C-CMR computes a virtual classifier θ′ by taking one SGD step on the new batch without replay, then scores buffered examples based on how much their loss increases post-update. This interference score s(m) identifies which examples are most at risk of forgetting due to the new data. E-BRS maintains a balanced class distribution in the replay buffer using entropy-based reservoir sampling, prioritizing retention of examples with high interference scores during eviction. These mechanisms jointly optimize for both selective replay and buffer integrity, addressing the limitations of vanilla ER in class-incremental settings. The failure mode occurs when the virtual classifier fails to capture true interference or when class imbalance is too severe for entropy balancing to suffice.
